cases.title: Job-search workspace
cases.brief: Find relevant roles, prepare applications and keep track of interviews.
cases.problem: A job search involves different resumes, job boards, application texts and follow-ups. The product keeps this work connected to the right profile and vacancy.
implementation: A browser interface for profiles, resumes, applications and interviews.
Queued vacancy search, matching and cover-letter preparation.
Profile-specific browser sessions and PostgreSQL records for prepared applications.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The preparation workflow saves application drafts with their vacancy, resume and supporting information. These records remain available for review; sending is a separate user-confirmed action.
cases.overview: The project covers the working steps between choosing a search profile and reviewing an application. A user can keep several resumes, search through a connected source, evaluate a vacancy and prepare a letter without losing the context used to write it. The same website contains the application board and administration area.
cases.audience: Job seekers managing several search directions and the operators maintaining the service.
cases.role: Architecture, browser interface, backend workflows, model integration and application records.

modules.title: Profiles and resumes
modules.text: A search uses an explicit profile and resume. Server checks verify ownership before reading resume content or saving an application.

modules.title: Vacancy preparation
modules.text: The worker searches a connected source, removes duplicate vacancy IDs and reads the selected vacancy before requesting a match assessment.

modules.title: Application drafts
modules.text: Matching and drafting are separate stages. A draft records its resume version, model and supporting evidence alongside the letter text.

modules.title: Search workspace
modules.text: The application list supports profile and status filters. Saved vacancy details, letters and interview screens keep the next action visible.

flow: Choose a profile and the resume for this search.
Search a connected source and assess relevant vacancies.
Prepare and save a letter for a selected vacancy.
Review the draft and track subsequent application activity.

engineering.title: Persistent background work
engineering.text: PostgreSQL stores queued work and prepared applications. Checkpoints let the worker verify its execution state between browser and model operations.

engineering.title: Resume-bound generation
engineering.text: A passing match assessment precedes drafting. Each draft retains its resume fingerprint and the facts used to write it.

deliverables: Web interface for the search and application workflow.
Search workers, preparation services and database persistence.
Administration screens and local deployment instructions.
cases.valueTitle: A clear next step for every opportunity
cases.valueText: A candidate can keep profiles, relevant vacancies, drafts and interview dates together. Reviewing a prepared application becomes a distinct step, with the vacancy and resume context close at hand.

cases.title: Campaign analytics
cases.brief: Campaign reports and an assistant that answers questions using connected data.
cases.problem: A media-buying team needs to compare accounts, campaigns and reporting periods without rebuilding the same analysis. An answer is useful only when the reader can identify its source, date range and permitted data.
implementation: Connected reporting data to a scheduled synchronization service and analytical workspace.
Built an assistant for questions about campaign data, with access controls, source notes and saved conversations.
Added team access, report presets and operational controls for administrators.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The workspace brings dashboards, detailed statistics and saved discussions together. Answers keep the reporting period and source visible.
cases.overview: The review starts with an overview of spend, revenue and profit. A user can follow a change into campaign or geographic breakdowns, then ask a focused question while keeping the reporting period visible.
cases.audience: Media buyers and team leads reviewing campaign performance and deciding what to investigate.
cases.role: Full-stack development across the reporting interface, API, data synchronization and assistant integration.

modules.title: Performance overview
modules.text: Summary cards and comparison periods establish context. Detail views group results by teams, buyers, campaigns and other available dimensions.

modules.title: Report workspace
modules.text: Filters, grouped dimensions and saved presets support recurring analysis. Data timestamps help the reader judge whether a report covers the intended period.

modules.title: Ask about campaign data
modules.text: The assistant selects permitted sources and explains a bounded set of results. Answers retain their source and period alongside the conversation history.

modules.title: Administration
modules.text: Operators can inspect synchronization, request logs and model usage. Versioned instructions let teams adjust answer style without expanding access to data.

flow: Choose a period and inspect the overview.
Open a breakdown and narrow the report.
Ask a question about the selected data.
Check the answer against its source and save the discussion.

engineering.title: One access boundary
engineering.text: The API applies team and owner scope before reading analytics. A question about another team cannot grant access to its records.

engineering.title: Traceable answers
engineering.text: PostgreSQL stores reporting snapshots and conversations. The assistant explains prepared evidence; it cannot change campaigns or advertising budgets.

deliverables: Responsive reporting workspace with reusable views.
Data synchronization and administration interface.
Assistant integration with saved, attributable answers.
cases.valueTitle: From campaign data to an answer
cases.valueText: A marketer can compare periods, inspect the numbers behind a report and ask a follow-up question in the same workspace. The answer stays connected to its source data.

cases.title: Campaign planning
cases.brief: Prepare campaign plans, review settings and track execution tasks.
cases.problem: Campaign preparation combines accounts, targeting, budgets and creative assignments. An operator needs to verify the complete configuration before execution and later identify which version was approved, who approved it and what happened to the job.
implementation: Built structured plans with validation and immutable configuration snapshots.
Connected administrator approval to the exact plan and execution queue.
Added workstation agents, status tracking and provider integration boundaries.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: Operators can prepare and approve a plan, then track its queued execution. The provider integration is demonstrated in a sandbox, with campaign objects kept paused.
cases.overview: A campaign begins as a structured plan. Review brings its budget, audience settings and creative assignments together. Approval applies to that exact snapshot, giving the operator a consistent reference throughout execution and troubleshooting.
cases.audience: Media buyers preparing campaign setups and administrators responsible for reviewing execution.
cases.role: Full-stack development of the planning interface, workflow API, persistence and workstation agent.

modules.title: Plan editor
modules.text: The form collects account context, targeting, budget and creative assignments. Validation checks required fields and whether ad-set budgets match the campaign total.

modules.title: Approval
modules.text: The review view exposes the saved configuration and its fingerprint. An administrator grants a short-lived, single-use approval for that specific version.

modules.title: Queue and status
modules.text: Jobs show whether work is waiting, claimed, running or finished with a recorded result. Operators can cancel work that remains in the queue.

modules.title: Workstation agents
modules.text: Each agent belongs to an owner and connection. Only a matching device can receive a job; provider credentials stay on the workstation.

flow: Enter campaign parameters and validate the plan.
Review the saved snapshot and approve it.
Assign a compatible agent through the queue.
Inspect the execution record before any activation.

engineering.title: Exact configuration
engineering.text: PostgreSQL preserves plans and job events. Hash-bound approval and idempotent submission link execution to the reviewed configuration and guard against duplicate jobs.

engineering.title: Bounded execution
engineering.text: Agents use leases and heartbeats to report progress. Successful creation requires a verified PAUSED result, leaving campaign activation to a human operator.

deliverables: Campaign planning and approval interface.
Persistent workflow API with execution records.
Workstation agent and sandbox demonstration flow.
cases.valueTitle: Review before execution
cases.valueText: A campaign plan can be checked and approved before execution jobs are created. Operators can inspect job status and history instead of treating a launch request as an invisible background action.

cases.title: Match analysis
cases.brief: Replay analysis for CS2 and Dota 2, with player reports and match events.
cases.problem: A replay contains events, participants and timing information, but a player needs a focused review of their own match. Useful analysis must keep calculated statistics connected to source events and show where the replay cannot support a conclusion.
implementation: Built replay upload, participant selection and background analysis.
Connected game-specific parsers to player reports and downloadable evidence.
Added report history, metric comparisons and paired English and Russian interfaces.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: A supported replay file produces a saved report for the selected player, with statistics linked to source events. Missing values remain visible, and compatible completed reports can be compared.
cases.overview: The user uploads a supported replay file and selects a participant. Background processing extracts the relevant events, calculates game-specific statistics and saves a report. The player can inspect the supporting data and compare compatible completed matches.
cases.audience: Individual CS2 and Dota 2 players reviewing their performance after a match.
cases.role: Web application and backend development across upload, processing, reports and data validation.

modules.title: Replay intake
modules.text: Upload checks cover file format, size and allowance. Content hashes identify duplicate replay files, while participant discovery helps users select the correct player.

modules.title: Background analysis
modules.text: A separate worker processes queued tasks through game adapters. Parsing and player-specific reporting are separate stages, allowing compatible parsed data to serve multiple participants.

modules.title: Player reports
modules.text: Reports combine measured statistics with source-linked observations. A downloadable evidence file keeps the underlying facts available for a closer review.

modules.title: History and comparison
modules.text: Saved reports support metric comparisons across matches. The comparison excludes explicitly incomplete results and keeps game and player identity consistent.

flow: Upload a supported CS2 or Dota 2 replay file.
Select the participant to analyse.
Follow processing into the saved player report.
Inspect the evidence and compare completed matches.

engineering.title: Reproducible processing
engineering.text: Parser and pipeline versions participate in result identity. Reusing a compatible parse avoids repeating the same extraction while preserving the relationship to its source.

engineering.title: Explicit data quality
engineering.text: Unknown values remain unknown. Validation checks provenance and rejects unsupported metrics; the interface keeps these limits visible instead of inventing complete statistics.

deliverables: English and Russian replay-review web interface.
Upload and background-processing backend with game adapters.
Player reports, history and downloadable supporting data.
cases.valueTitle: A match report you can inspect
cases.valueText: A player or analyst can move from a replay file to a personal report, then inspect the supporting events and tables. Structured data makes it easier to revisit the analysis and compare the underlying evidence.

cases.title: Sales team app
cases.brief: Daily sales, targets and training in an iPhone app for the team.
cases.problem: A sales team needs a place to record daily results, follow goals and access training.
implementation: SwiftUI dashboards, daily reporting, rankings and learning modules.
An authenticated API client with token refresh and typed responses.
A FastAPI backend with PostgreSQL, employee-specific data and calculation endpoints.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The app reads business data through the API and records daily submissions and learning progress.
cases.overview: A native workspace for a sales employee, with a connected backend for daily reporting, individual goals, learning and support. The project covers the mobile screens and the API that supplies them. Dashboard, reporting and training data use the same employee context, so the app can move between these tasks without asking the user to re-enter their details.
cases.audience: Sales employees and the managers responsible for their results and training.
cases.role: iOS interface, API integration, data models and backend endpoints.

modules.title: Dashboard and goals
modules.text: The start screen brings together the employee profile, current indicators and monthly targets. The user can review the current position before moving into daily reporting or a detailed calculation.

modules.title: Daily reporting
modules.text: A dedicated form records the day's results and sends them to the backend. The history keeps earlier submissions available for review, while rankings provide a separate view of team performance.

modules.title: Learning and updates
modules.text: Learning modules have saved progress. A news feed tracks read items, keeping training materials and internal updates within the same app as day-to-day work.

modules.title: Support and calculations
modules.text: The support area presents a personal contact and message history. Scenario calculations use structured inputs, so the screen can show the calculated result alongside the assumptions.

flow: Sign in and load the employee dashboard.
Review targets and enter the day's results.
Open the ranking or continue a learning module.
Return to saved results or contact support.

engineering.title: A typed client and a shared API
engineering.text: The Swift client uses asynchronous requests and typed responses. Authentication and token refresh are handled in the network layer, keeping that logic out of individual SwiftUI screens.

engineering.title: Business data belongs on the server
engineering.text: FastAPI routes and PostgreSQL models separate employees, reports and learning progress. Screens request the data they need through dedicated endpoints, while user context controls which records they can access.

deliverables: Native iOS screens for reporting, goals, learning and support.
An authenticated API client with refresh handling.
Backend routes and data models for the mobile workflows.
cases.valueTitle: One workspace for the sales team
cases.valueText: Employees can record results, check goals and find learning materials without switching between disconnected tools. Managers can work with structured reports rather than collecting updates in messages.

cases.title: Recipe app
cases.brief: Save recipes and follow each cooking step with a built-in timer.
cases.problem: A recipe needs to be convenient both when choosing a dish and while cooking it.
implementation: Recipe categories, ingredients and a step-by-step cooking view.
Locally saved favorites and a countdown timer with pause and resume.
Recipe sharing through the native iOS share sheet.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: Choose a recipe, save it to favorites, then open its cooking steps or start a timer.
cases.overview: An iOS recipe catalogue built around two moments: choosing what to cook and following the recipe in the kitchen. Categories and recipe details support the first step; a focused cooking view and timer support the second. The main content is bundled with the app, and favorites are kept on the device.
cases.audience: People who want to find a dish, keep useful recipes and follow preparation steps on an iPhone.
cases.role: SwiftUI screens, recipe models, local favorites and native sharing.

modules.title: Browse and choose
modules.text: Recipes are grouped by category and presented with an image and cooking time. Each detail screen brings ingredients and instructions together, so users can judge the recipe before starting.

modules.title: A personal shortlist
modules.text: A recipe can be added to favorites from its detail screen and opened again in a dedicated collection. The saved selection is restored when the app is opened later.

modules.title: Step-by-step cooking
modules.text: A separate cooking view shows the current instruction with forward and back controls. The navigation respects the first and last steps, keeping attention on the current part of the recipe.

modules.title: Timer and sharing
modules.text: The timer opens as its own sheet and supports starting, pausing and continuing the countdown. Recipes can also be passed to other apps through the standard iOS share sheet.

flow: Browse a category and open a recipe.
Review its ingredients and save it to favorites.
Open the cooking steps or start a timer.
Return to the saved recipe or share it.

engineering.title: One model for recipe content
engineering.text: The recipe model holds the title, image, cooking time, ingredients, steps and category. The catalogue, detail view and cooking mode consume this common structure rather than maintaining separate copies.

engineering.title: Local persistence with native presentation
engineering.text: Favorites are encoded and stored locally. SwiftUI sheets separate cooking, timing and sharing from the browsing screen, while the system share sheet provides familiar destinations.

deliverables: A native catalogue and complete recipe detail flow.
Persistent favorites and a focused cooking view.
A countdown timer and integration with iOS sharing.
cases.valueTitle: From choosing a dish to cooking it
cases.valueText: The same app supports browsing at leisure and following a recipe at the stove. A shortlist helps the user return to recipes; a focused step view keeps the current action easy to read.

cases.title: Inventory app
cases.brief: Track product batches, stock movements and quality checks on iPhone.
cases.problem: An egg-production inventory needs batch-level stock tracking, freshness checks and a movement history.
implementation: Batch creation, editing and archiving, with stock movement records.
Quantity validation, freshness indicators and quality checks.
Sales reports, weekly totals and local persistence.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: Recording a stock movement updates the batch quantity. Validation prevents removing more than is available.
cases.overview: An iOS stock-control application for egg production, with batch records, movements, quality checks and reports. The central object is the batch: its collection date, quantity, location and condition stay connected to subsequent events. A native WebKit integration is another part of the project, providing navigation and attachment selection for embedded web content.
cases.audience: Small producers who need to track batches, remaining stock, freshness and sales.
cases.role: SwiftUI interface, inventory calculations, local storage and WebKit integration.

modules.title: Batch records
modules.text: Create, edit or archive a batch with its collection date, starting quantity and storage location. Freshness indicators use configurable age thresholds, helping the user choose which stock to handle first.

modules.title: Stock movements
modules.text: Sales, usage, damage and other movement types update the current batch quantity. The movement history stays attached to the batch, making individual changes available for later review.

modules.title: Quality and reporting
modules.text: Quality checks are recorded alongside stock events. Reports group inventory by location and age, summarize weekly activity and calculate sales totals from recorded transactions.

modules.title: Web content inside iOS
modules.text: A SwiftUI wrapper hosts WKWebView with navigation, media support and system dialogs. On supported iOS versions, web upload requests can use the camera, photo library or document picker.

flow: Create a batch and record its initial stock.
Log a sale, usage or other stock movement.
Add a quality check and review freshness.
Open reports to inspect remaining stock and activity.

engineering.title: Validation before a stock change
engineering.text: The inventory logic checks positive quantities and rejects deductions larger than the available amount. Calculations are separated from the screens, so the dashboard and reports use the same definitions.

engineering.title: Local state and native web integration
engineering.text: Batch data, movements and settings are encoded into local storage. The WebKit layer handles web navigation and device interactions separately from the inventory logic; native attachment selection targets iOS 18.4 and later.

deliverables: Batch management, movement history and quality records.
Inventory metrics, reports and on-device persistence.
A native WebView shell with navigation and attachment handling.
cases.valueTitle: A traceable record for every batch
cases.valueText: Stock quantities, movements and quality observations stay attached to a batch. A small operation can see what was received, what changed and which checks were recorded without maintaining separate notes.

cases.title: WebView & native integration
cases.brief: Web content inside an iOS app, with native navigation and file access.
cases.problem: A web-based service needs access to the navigation, media and file-selection capabilities of an iPhone.
implementation: SwiftUI wrapper around WKWebView with back/forward controls and gestures.
Inline media, pop-up windows, external links and native alert dialogs.
Camera, photo library and document upload selection on supported iOS versions.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: Web content runs within an iOS shell. The upload chooser uses the native camera, photo library or file picker on iOS 18.4 and later.

cases.title: Product planning
cases.brief: Turn an app idea into requirements and a structured development brief.
cases.problem: An app concept needs more than a name. Screens, visual rules, data, testing and store materials need to describe the same product before implementation starts.
implementation: A guided workflow for selecting a visual theme, name and app concept.
Saved projects with document generation and ZIP export.
An Electron desktop shell running a local Next.js server and SQLite database.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The generation route assembles and saves a specification pack. The export endpoint produces a ZIP from the stored project choices and generation seed.
cases.overview: Web technology powers a local tool for organizing small iOS app ideas. Its output is a set of development documents covering the interface, data and checks for the implementation. The workflow connects an interactive wizard to server-side generation and downloadable files. The current application uses a single local user and stores projects on the computer.
cases.audience: Developers preparing a brief for an iOS project or a coding assistant.
cases.role: Interface development, generation logic, project storage, export endpoints and the desktop shell.

modules.title: Guided project setup
modules.text: The wizard carries the chosen theme, name, premise, main interaction and screen list into the saved project, together with the selected coding tool.

modules.title: Idea preparation
modules.text: Model responses have a defined JSON shape. The generator checks categories, required content and duplicate titles before returning candidate ideas.

modules.title: Project library
modules.text: SQLite stores the selected concept, metadata and generated brief. These fields provide the context for reopening a project and rebuilding its document pack.

modules.title: Document export
modules.text: The pack includes an overview, design system, components, screens, data model, QA checklist and store materials. ZIP export adds an entry-point README.

flow: Choose a visual direction and request candidate names.
Select an idea with its main interaction and screens.
Save the project and generate the development documents.
Download the pack for review and subsequent implementation.

engineering.title: One generation path
engineering.text: The preview and export endpoints use the same pack builder. A stored seed carries the selected variation into later exports.

engineering.title: Local desktop runtime
engineering.text: Electron starts the web server on loopback and gives the database a writable application-data directory, separate from packaged program files.

deliverables: Project wizard and saved-project interface.
Specification generator and downloadable document archive.
Local desktop runtime and packaging configuration.
cases.valueTitle: A brief that is ready for implementation work
cases.valueText: A developer can turn an initial idea into a coherent set of requirements and screen descriptions, then export the documents together. Saved projects can be reopened and their document packs exported again.

cases.title: Incubation planner
cases.brief: Batch schedules, daily readings and hatch records in an iPhone application.
cases.problem: Several batches can be at different stages of incubation. Dates, daily checks and observations need to stay connected to the right batch.
implementation: Batch planning with expected hatch dates and suggested candling and lockdown milestones.
Daily temperature, humidity and weight records, with notes and configurable range checks.
Hatch summaries, local storage and device reminders for active batches.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: Each batch keeps its schedule, observations and recorded outcome together. The dashboard shows due checks and approaching milestones.
cases.overview: The app follows a batch from its start date to the recorded hatch result. A keeper chooses the bird type, sets the incubation length and adds the batch details. The application calculates the schedule, while daily forms capture what the keeper actually observes. Reports then summarize those records by month and bird type.
cases.audience: Poultry keepers managing several incubation batches and wanting a consistent record of dates, conditions and outcomes.
cases.role: iOS development: screens, batch models, date calculations, local persistence and notification integration.

modules.title: Batch planning
modules.text: Create and edit batches with bird type, egg count, incubator, source and notes. Expected dates, current incubation day and progress remain tied to that batch.

modules.title: Daily checks
modules.text: Record temperature, humidity, turning, water checks and optional egg weight. Reading history supports charts and flags values outside the configured ranges.

modules.title: Candling records
modules.text: Log checked eggs and observations such as developing, clear or uncertain. Entries retain their batch and date for later review.

modules.title: Hatch results
modules.text: Record hatched and unhatched counts, notes and completion date. The batch moves to completed status and contributes to the result summaries.

flow: Create a batch and check its expected dates.
Follow today's checks and suggested milestones.
Add readings and candling observations as the batch develops.
Record the outcome and review the batch history.

engineering.title: One batch, linked records
engineering.text: Batch identifiers connect measurements, observations and outcomes. Date and rate calculations are separate from the SwiftUI views.

engineering.title: Local records and reminders
engineering.text: Codable state is saved on the device. Notification scheduling uses active batches and the keeper's reminder preferences.

deliverables: SwiftUI screens for batches, daily checks, observations, results and settings.
Data models and calculations for schedules, progress, weight changes and hatch rates.
Local persistence and configurable daily and milestone reminders.
cases.valueTitle: Daily checks with context
cases.valueText: The keeper can see what day a batch has reached, record readings and revisit earlier observations. Dates, reminders and hatch records form one timeline for each batch.

cases.title: Personal journal
cases.brief: Daily notes, personal goals and a clear view of changes over time.
cases.problem: A single note captures one moment. Reviewing changes over time requires consistent entries, dates and a way to compare them.
implementation: A daily entry with four rating sliders, a short note and a selected or written goal.
An archive with expandable entries, sorting and deletion confirmation.
Seven- and thirty-day views with charts, averages and rule-based summaries.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: A saved entry appears in the archive and contributes to the selected period's charts. Saving again on the same day replaces that day's entry.
cases.overview: This journal combines a daily form with earlier entries. Energy, focus, anxiety and sense of direction use consistent scales. A note and goal add context. The latest entry, archive and period view all use the same saved data.
cases.audience: People who want to keep brief personal notes and look back at their own ratings and goals over time.
cases.role: Native iOS development: entry forms, archive interactions, local persistence, chart drawing and summary calculations.

modules.title: Daily entry
modules.text: Four sliders accept self-ratings from zero to ten. The form includes a note of up to 140 characters and a goal selected from suggestions or entered as text.

modules.title: Entry archive
modules.text: Browse saved entries, expand a card and sort by date or calculated score. A confirmation dialog sits between selecting delete and removing a record.

modules.title: Trends and averages
modules.text: Switch between seven and thirty days, choose a metric and inspect an individual chart point. Averages summarize the entries in that period.

modules.title: Daily summary
modules.text: The home summary uses recent ratings to choose a predefined message. Goals and short notes keep the numerical view connected to the person's own words.

flow: Rate the day and add a short note and goal.
Save the entry or revise today's existing record.
Browse the archive and open an earlier entry.
Select a period and compare ratings on the charts.

engineering.title: A consistent daily record
engineering.text: A controller handles today's entry, updates and archive refreshes. Codable records are persisted locally with their dates and identifiers.

engineering.title: Explicit calculation rules
engineering.text: A separate analyzer computes averages and changes between groups of entries. SwiftUI paths and selectable points present the results without a charting dependency.

deliverables: Daily-entry, home, archive, trend and settings screens.
Local entry storage with same-day replacement and individual deletion.
Interactive charts, period filters and rule-based summary logic.
cases.valueTitle: A personal record that is easy to revisit
cases.valueText: Short daily entries create a history the user can browse by date or review as a trend. Ratings, notes and goals sit together so that a chart can be read alongside the context behind it.

cases.title: Poultry care journal
cases.brief: Daily care tasks, flock records and practical instructions in one iPhone app.
cases.problem: Looking after several bird groups involves feeding, cleaning, supplies and observations. Each task needs a place, a due date and a record of completion.
implementation: Coop and bird-group records linked to tasks, egg entries and observations.
Today's task list, feed quantities, low-stock thresholds and follow-up notes.
Egg-collection summaries and a set of care instructions that can be copied for a sitter.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The daily view gathers open tasks and recent activity. Recorded collections update the period totals, while supply quantities are compared with the configured thresholds.
cases.overview: The application organizes care around places and bird groups. Entries can belong to a specific coop or group, preserving their context. The main screen shows due work. Separate forms hold supplies, observations and instructions for someone taking over the routine.
cases.audience: Backyard poultry keepers and small homesteads managing multiple spaces, bird groups and daily care responsibilities.
cases.role: iOS development: linked data models, SwiftUI forms, daily views, summary calculations and local storage.

modules.title: Spaces and bird groups
modules.text: Record coops, brooders and other spaces with their status and cleaning interval. Bird groups have a type, breed, count and optional connection to a space.

modules.title: Daily task board
modules.text: Tasks carry a date, category, priority and related coop. The list separates due, upcoming and completed items, with templates for common chores.

modules.title: Supplies and observations
modules.text: Store feed quantities, units and low-stock thresholds. Care notes capture observations, actions taken and an optional date for a follow-up.

modules.title: Egg-collection history
modules.text: Log collection counts, damaged eggs and sizes against a date and group. The summary shows daily, weekly and monthly totals with a recent-days chart.

flow: Add the spaces and bird groups being cared for.
Create tasks with dates, priorities and a related space.
Record collections, supplies and observations during the routine.
Mark tasks complete or copy the written sitter instructions.

engineering.title: Records with context
engineering.text: Optional identifiers connect entries to a coop or bird group. The same records feed the daily view and the longer-term summaries.

engineering.title: Local state and derived totals
engineering.text: Codable state is saved in UserDefaults. Date filters, collection totals and low-stock indicators are calculated from the current records.

deliverables: Native screens for daily work, spaces, groups, collections and settings.
Forms for tasks, supplies, observations and sitter instructions.
Local storage and date-based summaries across related records.
cases.valueTitle: A consistent routine for everyday care
cases.valueText: Daily tasks, feed supplies and flock observations share the same records. Written care instructions make the routine easier to follow when the usual keeper is away.

cases.title: AI workflow automation
cases.brief: Agents that find information, use tools and prepare actions for human review.
cases.problem: A request may require several tools and decisions. The process needs to retain context, handle failed calls and distinguish actions that require approval.
implementation: Connected agents through shared state, routing and step limits in LangGraph.
Integrated external tools through function calling and MCP, with argument checks and retry handling.
Added approval points, regression evaluations and traces for investigating individual requests.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The workflow carries context between steps and resumes after human approval. Its tool choices and execution sequence can be inspected through traces and evaluation examples.
cases.overview: My work covered orchestration and backend integration for workplace assistants. A request could retrieve information, choose a tool and continue according to its result. I worked on the state and execution rules behind that sequence, including the points where a person must review an action.
cases.audience: Teams connecting AI assistants to internal information and working tools.
cases.role: Agent orchestration, tool integration, execution controls, evaluation and tracing.

modules.title: Context and routing
modules.text: Shared state carries retrieved information and intermediate results. Routing chooses the next step, with a limit on how long execution can continue.

modules.title: Tool calls
modules.text: Function calling and MCP connect external capabilities. Argument checks, retries and fallback paths handle invalid inputs or failed tool responses.

modules.title: Human approval
modules.text: Irreversible operations require confirmation. The workflow retains its context while waiting and continues from that context after the decision.

modules.title: Evaluation and traces
modules.text: Regression examples check answers, tool selection and action order. Langfuse and OpenTelemetry help locate failures within an individual request.

flow: Submit a request and retrieve the relevant context.
Select a tool and check its arguments.
Review an action when human approval is required.
Inspect the result and its execution trace.

engineering.title: Explicit execution rules
engineering.text: Shared state links successive calls, and step limits bound the run. Idempotency handles repeated requests; error rules define when to retry, fall back or wait for a decision.

engineering.title: Changes checked against examples
engineering.text: Prompt and model versions are compared on regression cases. Routing and caching changes are considered alongside answer quality, cost and latency.

deliverables: Agent orchestration and backend tool integrations.
Approval, retry and fallback handling.
Regression evaluations and request tracing.
cases.valueTitle: A process people can follow and review
cases.valueText: A multi-step request has an execution history and defined approval points. The team can investigate what the assistant did and where a decision needs human input.

cases.title: Document search
cases.brief: Find answers across internal documents, with references to the source material.
cases.problem: A useful document assistant must find relevant material before generating an answer. It also needs a clear response when the available context is insufficient.
implementation: Prepared documents, split them into passages and generated embeddings for retrieval.
Combined BM25 and vector search with reranking to select relevant context.
Connected retrieval to answer generation, source references and quality checks.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The retrieval workflow supplies relevant document fragments to generation. Answers include source references, allowing the reader to open the material and check the response.
cases.overview: My contribution covered the search and model integration behind a document assistant. I worked on preparing the collection, selecting context and connecting it to generation. The same work included response checks, prompt and model versions, and participation in local inference deployment and error monitoring.
cases.audience: Teams looking for answers in a collection of working documents.
cases.role: Document preparation, retrieval, model integration and answer evaluation.

modules.title: Document preparation
modules.text: Documents are divided into passages and represented with embeddings. This prepares the material for search at the level of relevant fragments.

modules.title: Hybrid retrieval
modules.text: BM25 searches for matching terms while vector retrieval finds related meaning. Reranking helps select the passages passed to the model.

modules.title: Answers with sources
modules.text: Generation uses the retrieved context. Source references connect the response to the document passages a reader can inspect alongside the answer.

modules.title: Insufficient context
modules.text: The workflow handles questions the retrieved material cannot adequately support. These cases also inform checks when prompts or models change.

flow: Ask a question about the document collection.
Retrieve and rerank potentially relevant passages.
Read an answer with its source references.
Open the source material to check the response.

engineering.title: Retrieval before generation
engineering.text: Document preparation and search determine the context available to the model. Looking at retrieved passages helps separate search problems from generation problems.

engineering.title: Evaluation and local inference
engineering.text: Answer quality is checked as prompt and model versions change. Local inference and error monitoring support investigation of the resulting service behavior.

deliverables: Document preparation and hybrid retrieval components.
Answer generation with source references.
Quality checks and local inference integration work.
cases.valueTitle: An answer with material to check
cases.valueText: The reader can move from a question to an answer and then to its supporting passage. The source remains available when the wording needs closer review.

cases.title: 1C development & integrations
cases.brief: Contracts, payments, reporting and data exchange across business systems.
cases.problem: Accounting changes must fit existing rules and data. Integrations also need to handle interrupted delivery and repeated messages without losing track of processing.
implementation: Developed customer-side changes for lease contracts, payment schedules and parallel accounting.
Built reconciliation reports and worked on budget limits and request approval routes.
Connected 1C exchanges through RabbitMQ, HTTP/REST, EnterpriseData and data-conversion rules.
cases.whatResultIsVerified: The work includes accounting extensions, reports and system exchanges. Message processing uses acknowledgement after writing, idempotency and explicit retry handling.
cases.overview: This case brings together separate assignments from my 1C practice: accounting changes and integration work. On the lease-accounting project, another contractor supplied the methodology and standard module. My role covered customer-side development, exchanges, reports, testing and acceptance of the changes within the existing system.
cases.audience: Businesses extending 1C accounting processes or connecting them to operational systems.
cases.role: Customer-side 1C development across accounting changes, reports and integrations.

modules.title: Contracts and payments
modules.text: Changes covered lease contracts, payment schedules, security deposits and contract modifications, together with the records needed for parallel accounting.

modules.title: Limits and approvals
modules.text: Separate assignments covered budget limits by item and cost center, plus request approval routes in the document-management system.

modules.title: Reconciliation reports
modules.text: Reports built with the 1C Data Composition System support reconciliation. Data exchanges connect the accounting, budgeting and operational systems involved.

modules.title: Message exchanges
modules.text: RabbitMQ integration acknowledges messages after writing. Idempotency, retries and an undelivered-message queue define how unsuccessful processing is handled.

flow: Define the accounting or exchange behavior required by the assignment.
Review the existing configuration and relevant data.
Implement the report, accounting change or exchange component.
Test the agreed scenario and prepare it for acceptance.

engineering.title: Changes within existing systems
engineering.text: Configuration extensions, standard libraries and data-conversion rules support the required changes. The implementation respects the boundaries of the standard accounting solution.

engineering.title: Processing and performance
engineering.text: Technological logs help locate slow operations. Query and index changes, managed locks and batch processing address the identified causes.

deliverables: 1C extensions and accounting-process changes.
Reconciliation reports and data-exchange components.
Testing, acceptance support and technical instructions.
cases.valueTitle: Accounting and exchanges with clear rules
cases.valueText: The work supports structured contract and payment records, reconciled data and exchanges that can be retried. Each assignment fits the business process and configuration it extends.
